content: The document titled Consolidated HIV Strategic Information Guidelines: Driving Impact Through Programme Monitoring and Management was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2020. It includes a Web Annex (Annex C) that provides additional indicators for monitoring and evaluating HIV-related programs. The publication is available electronically under the ISBN 978-92-4-000438-2 and is licensed under Creative Commons for non-commercial use, provided proper citation is given. The WHO logo cannot be used, and any adaptations of the work must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. The original English version remains the authoritative edition. It is calculated by dividing the number of individuals who discontinued PrEP due to toxicity (numerator) by the total number of individuals on PrEP during the reporting period (denominator). 2. Opioid Substitution Therapy (OST) Retention: This indicator tracks the percentage of individuals receiving OST who remain in treatment for at least six months. It is calculated by dividing the number of individuals still in treatment six months after starting OST (numerator) by the total number of individuals who started OST during the defined cohort recruitment period (denominator). 3. HIV Service Coverage in Prisons: Subcategories include: The number of clean needles and syringes distributed to prisoners. The number of prisoners receiving OST. The number of condoms distributed to prisoners. The number of prisoners receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART). The number of prisoners tested for HIV. The number or percentage of prisoners living with HIV. The number or percentage of prisoners with hepatitis C or co-infected with HIV and hepatitis C. 4. ARV Medicine Stock-Outs: It is calculated by dividing the number of ART sites with stock-outs (numerator) by the total number of reporting ART sites (denominator). 5. Early Infant Diagnosis (EID) Turnaround Time: This indicator tracks the percentage of EID test results returned within four weeks of specimen collection. It is calculated by dividing the number of EID tests conducted with results returned within four weeks (numerator) by the total number of EID tests conducted during the reporting period (denominator). A two-day turnaround time is considered an acceptable alternative in some contexts. 6. HPV Vaccination Coverage Among Women Living with HIV: It is calculated by dividing the number of women living with HIV who completed the vaccine series (numerator) by the estimated number of female survey respondents living with HIV (denominator). 7. Discriminatory Attitudes Toward People Living with HIV (PLHIV): It is assessed by asking survey respondents whether they would buy fresh vegetables from a vendor known to have HIV or whether they believe a teacher with HIV should be allowed to continue teaching. Respondents who answer no to either question are considered to hold discriminatory attitudes. The publication is part of WHO's broader effort to provide transparent and evidence-based guidelines for improving HIV program monitoring and management. It aligns with the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd edition, 2014).
